decisions.originalTitle: The God Who Documents His Grief (and teaches you to read your story by His)
decisions.displayTitle: Does Yahweh Grieve? What His Tears Teach You About Your Own Story
decisions.promoDescription: This lesson shows how Scripture records Yahweh's own grief, from Genesis to the tears of Jesus, so that believers can trust Him with their pain. It then teaches a practical method, modeled by Joseph, for reading your own memories, both good and hard, in light of what the Word reveals about Yahweh's hand.

decisions.originalTitle: The House of El — the Borrowed Name and the Only Saviour
decisions.displayTitle: Whose Name Are You Really Calling On?
decisions.promoDescription: This lesson examines the "El" in Superman's birth name and shows how the Word uses that same word for Yahweh, with Yahweh alone as the true Saviour. It contrasts a fictional rescuer who cannot be hurt with the Son who saved by giving His life, and it shows how to test such stories by Scripture.

decisions.imagePrompt: Cinematic 16:9 photograph of a Black woman in her forties, kneeling in a sunlit vegetable garden beside a raised wooden bed, gently sifting rich, crumbly soil through her fingers and smiling with calm, focused attention. She wears a bold cobalt blue cardigan. She is positioned in the right half of the frame in a medium close-up, her face sharp, expressive and well lit with eyes clearly visible. Lush green leafy plants and healthy young sprouts surround her, with a softly blurred background of open sky and a bright white garden fence. Bright natural daylight from the side, high-key exposure, soft open shadows, neutral white balance, true-to-life skin tones, vivid natural greens and blues, full-frame camera look, shallow depth of field, 85mm lens. The left third is bright, open and uncluttered for a headline. No text, letters, numbers, logos or signage anywhere in the image.
